correctness.rationale: The classes E_i, L_ij and the unique conic give off-diagonal intersection numbers 0 or 1, so intersecting smooth components meet transversely. No three can meet: the graph of disjoint index pairs and their incidences with exceptions and the conic has no triangles. It is connected with 16 vertices, 40 edges and genus 25. The fixed conic splits degree off the Laplacian cokernel. Its rooted reduced Laplacian is symmetric and Frobenius-equivariant, so its rational inverse defines a Frobenius-invariant perfect pairing modulo Z on the torsion cokernel; thus the fixed group is dual to the coinvariants. Independently formed the full integral relation matrix [L | σ−I] on even subsets of five labels (adjacency: symmetric difference of size four), computed exact Smith forms, and split off the single free degree factor. All seven torsion lists match, including (8,32) versus (2,4,32) at order 256. Raynaud's regular semistable component-group description is equivariant and the rational points of the finite étale group scheme are the Frobenius invariants, so this verifies the conditional interpretation without assuming split components.
residual_risks: The table classifies the specified S5 action fixing the conic, not all Weyl-group twists. It does not assert realization at every q or existence of a smoothing. The component-group statement only uses regular semistable smoothings with unit thickness.

value.rationale: The full exceptional boundary is natural, and the seven cases are the complete base-point permutations, not selected small examples. The exact invariant factors are needed to distinguish rational component-group structures that a component count alone cannot distinguish. The two order-256 rows provide a concrete instance, and the same table can be used in every regular unit-thickness smoothing with this boundary.
residual_risks: This value does not rest on the previously tabulated split row, or on any promised extension to other quartic twists.
